_about: PuffPAI offline workout library. Programs follow published exercise-science guidance (sources listed per program). Not medical advice — consult a physician before starting a new program. Optional web refresh can extend this library later; the base always works offline.
_ids: Every resistance exercise carries an 'id' matching the dashboard's EXERCISE_DB (app/_lib/fitnessScience.ts). That id is what fit_log_set stores, so a session picked from this library round-trips into FitFam history, PRs and Epley 1RMs without a name-matching step. Play/cardio items have no id on purpose: there is nothing to load-log.

functional_system.title: Functional Strength System
functional_system.audience: A sample five-day program for a small home kit. Equipment: 35 lb kettlebell · 2 x 25 lb dumbbells · pull-up bar · 20 kg barbell + 2 x 25 lb plates · ruck pack + 2 x 10 lb plates
functional_system.guidance: Three time tiers per training day: Full 45-55 min, Express 20-25 min, Minimum 12-15 min. None of them is a compromise, intensity and consistency beat volume. Progression is reps before rounds, rounds before weight. On express work the last 1-2 reps of every set must be genuinely hard. The barbell has exactly two settings ,  44 lb bare or 94 lb with both plates ,  so pick one load and stay there for the session; no plate juggling. Squats and hinges at 94 lb are light for a trained lifter, so tempo, pauses and higher reps are what make them bite; pressing at 94 lb is real strength work.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Row
exercises.notes: Bare 44 lb bar. This version is for grooving the sequence, so every rep is a technique rep.

exercises.name: Hang Power Clean
exercises.notes: Explosive hip snap to the rack position. The light bar is the point here, get the timing right.

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.notes: Straight out of the rack position, elbows high.

exercises.name: Push Press
exercises.notes: Leg drive overhead, not strict. Strict press is fine at this weight if you want it.

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Lower the bar behind your neck, then squat. Rest 90 seconds, that is the round. Four rounds. Move up to 94 lb once the chain feels smooth.

exercises.name: KB Swings (odd minutes)
exercises.notes: Every minute on the minute: start at the top of each odd minute and rest with whatever is left.

exercises.name: Pull-Ups (even minutes)
exercises.notes: Top of each even minute, straight into the push-ups.

exercises.name: Ruck
exercises.notes: Two 10 lb plates, pack and water, about 22-25 lb. Weeks 1-2: 20-25 min, easy pace, flat. Weeks 3-4: 30-40 min with gentle hills. Weeks 5-6: 45-60 min, varied terrain, conversational zone-2 pace. After that, add load or pace only if it feels easy. Duration first, same as your lifting.

exercises.name: Cool-Down Walk
exercises.notes: Drop the pack and walk it off. Watch your shoulders and lower back the first week. If the pack digs or your posture breaks down, drop weight or time.

readiness_minimalist.title: Readiness Minimalist
readiness_minimalist.audience: Experienced lifter, home gym: bodyweight, pull-up bar, a fixed 45 lb Olympic bar (no plates), one ~35 lb kettlebell
sources: ACSM Position Stand: Progression Models in Resistance Training for Healthy Adults (Med Sci Sports Exerc)
Schoenfeld et al.: Effects of Load on Muscular Adaptations, 6-20+ rep loads grow muscle when taken near failure (J Strength Cond Res)
Pak/Grgic: Effort and time-under-tension as progression levers when external load is fixed
readiness_minimalist.guidance: No fixed weekly split, the engine picks train/light/rest from daily readiness. Load is deliberately light (45 lb bar, 35 lb KB), so progression is reps, tempo, density, single-arm/unilateral loading, and bodyweight skill steps, NOT plates. Take working sets to RPE 8; when you clear the top of a rep range with clean form, advance the movement (harder variation, slower tempo, or hang the KB) rather than hunting for weight you do not own.

exercises.name: Strict Overhead Press
exercises.notes: 45 lb bar. Keep your legs still and let your shoulders do the pressing, no bouncing to help it up. Since the weight's fixed, get stronger by pausing at your forehead and lowering slowly over about 3 seconds before you add a set.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Bodyweight. Once you can do 20 clean reps, make it harder with feet-up or one-sided push-ups. That's how you progress here, not by adding weight.

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.notes: Bodyweight on bars or between two solid surfaces. Lower yourself slowly, about 3 seconds; once 12 reps feel easy, hang the 35 lb kettlebell from a belt for more.

exercises.name: Single-Arm KB Press
exercises.notes: 35 lb kettlebell, one arm at a time. The weight's on one side, so it'll try to tip you over. That's the point. Stay tall and even, don't lean.

exercises.name: KB Lateral Raise
exercises.notes: One arm with the 35 lb kettlebell, or something lighter. Raise slowly with no swinging. You're after the burn, not how high it goes.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
exercises.notes: Bodyweight, from a full hang up to your chin over the bar. Once you can do 12 clean reps, hang the 35 lb kettlebell from a belt to make it harder.

exercises.name: Barbell Row
exercises.notes: 45 lb bar, upper body bent forward. The weight's fixed, so add reps, squeeze for a second at the top, and lower the bar back down slowly.

exercises.name: Single-Arm KB Row
exercises.notes: 35 lb kettlebell, one arm, with your other hand braced on a bench or knee. Let it stretch all the way down, then pull your elbow back toward your hip.

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
exercises.notes: 45 lb bar. No swinging, lower it slowly over about 3 seconds and squeeze hard at the top, and even a light bar gives you plenty.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.notes: Use a band, or row a bar or rings toward your face. Hold the squeeze for a second at the end. This keeps the backs of your shoulders healthy.

exercises.name: Tempo Front Squat
exercises.notes: 45 lb bar held across the front of your shoulders. Lower over 3 seconds, pause 1 second at the bottom, stand up in 1, a light bar moved slowly is not an easy set. Swap in goblet squats if the front hold is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: KB Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.notes: Your best friend when weight is limited, hold the 35 lb kettlebell at your chest, or in one hand down at your side. Add reps, then lower slowly and pause at the bottom so you never miss having more weight.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: 45 lb bar. Push your hips back and feel the stretch down the back of your thighs, go for a good stretch and a full pause at the bottom, not a big number.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.notes: 35 lb kettlebell. Snap your hips forward hard and stand tall and straight at the top. This builds power and gets you breathing. Keep every rep sharp.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.notes: Hanging from the pull-up bar. Start with bent knees; once you can do 15 clean, move to straight-leg raises.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.notes: 35 lb kettlebell, slow and deliberate, settle into every position. This builds whole-body control and steady shoulders; go for quality, not speed.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.notes: 35 lb kettlebell at a steady, breathless pace. Keep snapping your hips sharply even when you're breathing hard.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.notes: 35 lb kettlebell, one in each hand if you have two, otherwise carry one at your side like a suitcase and switch hands each round. Stand tall, ribs down.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: 35 lb kettlebell held at your chest. Stay upright, squat all the way down, stay controlled. Keep your rests short so it stays challenging.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.notes: Squeeze your core and glutes tight. Once 60 seconds feels easy, add time or slow shoulder taps.

intermediate_strength.title: Upper/Lower Strength Split
sources: ACSM Position Stand: Progression Models in Resistance Training for Healthy Adults (Med Sci Sports Exerc)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed.
intermediate_strength.guidance: 3-4 sets, 6-12 reps for hypertrophy or 4-6 for strength emphasis; 2-3 min rest on compound lifts; progress load ~2-5% when all sets hit the top of the rep range at RPE 8 or below.

beginner_general.title: Full-Body Foundations
beginner_general.audience: Adults, new or returning to exercise
sources: ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. (150 min/wk moderate aerobic + 2x/wk resistance)
WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour (2020)
beginner_general.guidance: Start 1-2 sets of 10-15 reps at a comfortable load; add a set after two consistent weeks; a brisk 10-min walk warm-up counts toward the weekly aerobic target.

youth_developmental.title: Teen Athletic Development
youth_developmental.audience: Adolescents, technique first, no max lifts, adult supervision recommended
sources: NSCA Position Statement on Youth Resistance Training (Lloyd et al., J Strength Cond Res)
AAP Council on Sports Medicine: Strength Training by Children and Adolescents (Pediatrics)
youth_developmental.guidance: 1-2 sets of 10-15 reps with bodyweight or light loads; master form before adding weight; NO one-rep-max attempts; emphasize movement quality, speed, and fun.

active_play.title: Adventure Hour for Kids
active_play.audience: Children, activity through play, not structured lifting
sources: WHO: children 5-17 should average 60 min/day of moderate-to-vigorous activity
CDC Physical Activity Guidelines for School-Age Children
active_play.guidance: Make it a game. Mix running, climbing, balancing, throwing, and dancing. Muscle- and bone-strengthening play (hopping, climbing) at least 3 days a week.
